"''Trust me, I've got no interest in being a hero, Commodore, what I—''"
"''Well, congratulations. You're not one.|Almudin, to Han Solo, during the latter's court martial|audio=AlmudinAndSolo-Maverick.flac|}} '''Almudin''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] who served as a [[commodore]] in the [[Galactic Empire]]. In [[10 BBY]], Almudin was part of a [[Imperial Military|military]] tribunal and oversaw the [[Tribunal of Han Solo|court martial]] of [[Imperial cadet]] [[Han Solo]], who had disobeyed orders during an [[Attack on Onyx Squadron|attack]] by raiders on [[Onyx Squadron]], which he was [[Pilot|flying]] in at the [[time]], to save the life of [[Cadet]] [[Lyttan Dree]]. The court martial resulted in Solo's expulsion from the [[Carida Academy|flight academy]] at [[Carida]] and the [[Imperial Navy]], thereafter reassigning him to the [[224th Imperial Armored Division]] on [[Mimban]]. It was rumored that Almudin had an amazing flight record before his assignment on the tribunal. ==Biography== {{Quote|This tribunal, me in particular, finds you guilty of disobeying a direct order, and you are hereby reassigned to the infantry. Report for immediate transfer to Mimban.|Almudin sentences Han Solo|audio=Almudin-Guilty.flac|}} [[File:Han_Solo_Trial.png|thumb|left|250px|Almudin (center) at Han Solo's military tribunal]] [[Commodore]] Almudin was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] who served in the [[Imperial Navy]] of the [[Galactic Empire]]. In [[10 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' states that [[Han Solo]] was expelled from the [[Imperial Navy]] in [[10 BBY]]. Almudin had the job of sentencing Navy [[pilot]]s at [[Imperial Military|military]] tribunals and was one of the [[Imperial officer]]s present for the [[Tribunal of Han Solo|tribunal]] of [[Imperial cadet]] [[Han Solo]], a student at the [[Carida Academy|Imperial flight academy]] on the [[planet]] [[Carida]] and a member of [[Onyx Squadron]]. Solo had disobeyed a direct order during a [[Attack on Onyx Squadron|dogfight]] with raiders in order to save fellow cadet [[Lyttan Dree]], who was flying under the [[callsign]] [[Onyx Two]]. At the tribunal, Almudin had Solo recount the events of the mission in which he had saved Onyx Two, even though the details were all included in the cadet's report. Almudin and the other [[officer]]s present, including [[Warrant Officer]] [[Ardwyl Hercho]],''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story The Official Guide]]'' proceeded to find Solo guilty of disobeying a direct order and reassigned him to the [[224th Imperial Armored Division]] of the [[Imperial Army]], which was [[Mimban Campaign|fighting]] on the planet [[Mimban]]. Solo later deserted and became a criminal and wished that Almudin was with him while he was making a record breaking [[Kessel Run]] with a cargo of unrefined [[coaxium]]. The former cadet doubted that the commodore would have been impressed with his skills, but would have prefered to have had Almudin there to [[Death|die]] with him if the coaxium exploded, although ultimately, Solo successfully completed the run with the coaxium intact. ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|Cadet Solo. I still can't decide if you're brave or stupid.''"
"''I like to think I'm a little of both, sir. I mean, Moff. Sir Moff.''"
"''It's 'Commodore,' and if you think having a smart-ass attitude is the way to go here, you're sorely mistaken.|Almudin and Han Solo|audio=AlmudinAndSolo-SmartAss.flac|}} [[File:Almudin-Solo1.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Almudin was rumored to have had an impressive flight record.]] Almudin had a particularly round face, which Han Solo found distracting and irritating during his military tribunal. Almudin spoke to the cadet with a tone of less than disgust and, upon sentencing, made sure to note that he in particular found Solo guilty. When Solo forgot the commodore's rank, Almudin initially did not change his expression as Solo tried to correct himself but finally broke as the cadet finished. Interpreting the cadet's words as mockery, Almudin warned him that being a "smart ass" would not help his cause. Solo had heard rumor that Almudin had an amazing flight record prior to his tribunal assignments. The commodore had [[Color|tan]] skin, graying black [[hair]], and brown [[eye]]s. He spoke [[Galactic Basic Standard]] with an aristocratic accent.[[Solo: A Star Wars Story: Expanded Edition (audiobook)|''Solo: A Star Wars Story: Expanded Edition'' audiobook]] ==Equipment== Almudin wore a gray [[Imperial military uniforms|Imperial officer's uniform]] with four [[code cylinder]]s and a [[rank insignia plaque]]. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|This tribunal sees no reason to ''terminate'' a well-trained, if defiant, cadet. Therefore, we recommend transferring you to the tip of the spear on Mimban. Active duty immediately.|Almudin's altered dialogue in the ''Solo: A Star Wars Story'' comic adaptation|}} [[File:SoloTribunal-Solo1.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Almudin's dialogue was slightly altered in the comic adaptation of ''Solo''.]] Almudin was created for the [[2018]] [[Star Wars Anthology Series|Anthology]] film, ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]''; however, the sole scene including the character was cut from the final release. Despite this, the scene appeared in various adaptations of the film, starting with ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story: Expanded Edition]]'', a novelization written by [[Mur Lafferty]] and released on [[September 4]], 2018.{{PenguinRandomHouse|url=books/574532/solo-a-star-wars-story-expanded-edition-by-mur-lafferty/9780525619390|text=Solo: A Star Wars Story: Expanded Edition}} The novel adaptation of the scene bore only slight differences in dialogue from the film's script. The [[Solo: A Star Wars Story: Expanded Edition (audiobook)|audiobook]] of the novel also differs slightly from both the film and novel, as Almudin's use of the term "smart-ass" is removed. The scene was depicted for the first time in the [[Solo: A Star Wars Story Adaptation 1|first issue]] of the [[Solo: A Star Wars Story Adaptation|comic adaptation]] of ''Solo'', released on [[October 10]], 2018,{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/73027/solo_a_star_wars_story_adaptation_2018_1|text=Solo: A Star Wars Story Adaptation (2018) #1}} and written by [[Robbie Thompson]] with illustrations by [[Will Sliney]]. The depiction of the military tribunal in the [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] adaptation differs in several ways from the film script and novelization, including Almudin's dialogue. This article assumes that the dialogue from novelization takes precedence in [[canon]] over the comic adaption. The scene itself, in which Almudin was portrayed by [[Ramon Tikaram]], who previously declined the role of [[Quarsh Panaka]] in the [[1999]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']],{{WebCite|url=https://www.fanthatracks.com/news/film-music-tv/solo-a-star-wars-story-ramon-tikaram-and-missing-out-twice-on-star-wars|text=Solo: A Star Wars Story: Ramon Tikaram and missing out twice on Star Wars|author=[[Mark Newbold]]|date=2018-09-14|work=[https://www.fanthatracks.com Fantha Tracks]|archivedate=20191208211016}} was then included as a deleted scene on the [[Star Wars home video releases|home-video release]] of the film. Due to its inclusion in the novelization, this article treats the deleted scene as also being canonical. The novelization and the 2018 [[Solo: A Star Wars Story: A Junior Novel|junior novelization]] of the film by [[Joe Schreiber]]''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story: A Junior Novel]]'' both include Solo thinking of Almudin while making the Kessel Run; however, in the novelization the mention is presented as Solo merely thinking of the commodore, whereas in the junior novel he mentions Almudin to his allies [[Chewbacca]] and [[Tobias Beckett]] in dialogue, incorrectly calling Almudin a [[captain]] rather than a commodore. This article makes no assumptions about which of these versions of events is canon beyond the fact that Solo wished Almudin was there. ==Appearances== {{Mediacat|soundcat=Audio files of Almudin|imagecat=Images of Almudin}} *''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]'' {{Del}} *''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story: Expanded Edition]]'' {{Ab|Solo: A Star Wars Story: Expanded Edition (audiobook)}} {{1st}} *''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story: A Junior Novel]]'' {{Ab|Solo: A Star Wars Story: A Junior Novel (audiobook)}} {{Mo}} *[[Solo: A Star Wars Story Adaptation 1|''Solo: A Star Wars Story Adaptation'' 1]] ==Notes and references== {{Reflist}} {{Interlang |fi=Almudin |ka=ალმუდინი }} [[Category:Humans]] [[Category:Imperial Navy officers of the Galactic Empire]] [[Category:Individuals with he/him pronouns]] [[Category:Males]]
